# Sirach Chapter 45 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 45 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_045_page_001.jpg

---

45:1 From him he brought forth a man who found favor in the sight of all the living, beloved of God and men — Moses, whose memory is blessed.

45:2 He made him equal in glory to the holy ones, and made him great in the awesome fear of his enemies.

45:3 By his words he caused signs to cease; he glorified him in the sight of kings, and gave him commandments for his people, and showed him part of his glory.

45:4 He sanctified him through faithfulness and meekness; he chose him out of all flesh.

45:5 He made him hear his voice, and led him into the thick cloud, and gave him commandments face to face, the law of life and knowledge, so that he might teach Jacob the covenant and Israel his judgments.

45:6 He exalted Aaron, a holy man like him, his brother, of the tribe of Levi.

45:7 He made an everlasting covenant with him, and gave him the priesthood of the people; he blessed him with splendor and girded him with a glorious belt.

45:8 He clothed him with perfect glory and fortified him with the emblems of strength: the linen undergarments, the long robe, and the ephod.

45:9 And he encircled him with pomegranates and with very many golden bells all around, to send out a sound as he walked, to make their sound heard in the temple as a reminder to the children of his people.

45:10 With a sacred garment of gold and blue and purple, the work of an embroiderer; with the oracle of judgment, the Urim and Thummim;

45:11 with twisted crimson, the work of a craftsman; with precious stones engraved like a seal, in a setting of gold, the work of a jeweler, as a memorial according to the number of the tribes of Israel;

45:12 with a gold crown upon his turban, engraved with the seal of holiness, a glory of honor and a work of strength, a delight for the eyes, beautiful beyond measure.

45:13 Before him there was nothing like these things. No outsider ever wore them; only his sons, and his descendants perpetually.

45:14 His sacrifices were wholly consumed, twice a day continually.

45:15 Moses filled his hands and anointed him with holy oil; it was an everlasting covenant for him and for his seed as long as the heavens last, to serve as priest and to praise him and bless his name.

45:16 He chose him out of all the living to offer sacrifice to the Lord, incense and a pleasing aroma as a memorial portion, to make atonement for the people.

45:17 In his commandments he gave him authority and statute in judgments, to teach Jacob the testimonies and to enlighten Israel in his law.

45:18 Strangers banded against him and envied him in the wilderness — the men of Dathan and Abiram and the assembly of Korah, with fury and wrath.

45:19 The Lord saw it and was not pleased, and they were destroyed in the heat of his anger; he worked wonders against them to consume them in his flaming fire.

45:20 But he made the glory of Aaron great and gave him his inheritance: the firstfruits of the harvest he allotted to him.

45:21 He prepared bread for them in abundance, for the priests they eat the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave to him and his seed.

45:22 But in the land of the people he has no inheritance, and he has no portion among the people, for the Lord himself is his portion and inheritance.

45:23 Phinehas the son of Eleazar is third in glory, zealous in the fear of the Lord, and he stood firm when the people turned away, in the noble readiness of his soul; and he made atonement for Israel.

45:24 Therefore a covenant of peace was established for him, to be leader of the sanctuary and of his people, so that he and his descendants should have the dignity of the priesthood forever.

45:25 A covenant was also made with David the son of Jesse, of the tribe of Judah, an inheritance to the king alone from son to son; so the inheritance of Aaron is for his descendants alone.

45:26 Now may God grant you wisdom in your heart to judge his people in righteousness, so that their good things may not be abolished, and that their glory may endure for all their generations.
